notes.title: v18: Settings Update
notes.content:
Hi all, hope you are having a good summer. After spending five months working on the Puffin Planes Planes Update, I decided to try and keep the scope for v18 smaller. It's kind of a grab bag of random tweaks and features so I'm just going to name it the Settings Update, after the new game settings overhaul.


4 New Soundtracks from Rodnie Vue
Rodnie has been fantastic to work with on the soundtrack for Puffin Planes. Let's hear from him about the four new tracks that he has hand-crafted for the game:

Vestmannaeyjar - This archipelago off the south coast of Iceland is known for its big puffin population; I'd imagine those puffins would be chatting a lot with each other.

Saxopuffins - I think puffins are the type of creatures to really like ambient saxophone music...

Beak into the Sea - Like many other seabirds, puffins dive into the ocean to hunt small fish for food, maybe even catching a glimpse of the underwater world.

Clifftops - Maybe puffins are like humans, wondering about the world on top of distant cliffs.

You can listen to these soundtracks in-game. If you love the tracks and want to take them with you, let us know! Maybe we can get Rodnie to upload the music to Spotify, Bandcamp or somewhere else.


Better Version Management
Some of you might not like my updates (I guess the game was already perfect), or maybe you are still working on a campaign in the older version. If so, I've improved the version management to enable you to play any previous major version (v17, v16 or v15).

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/d2ba71324818f21470a087967aa70c7cc7a79ba0.png"]


Manufacturer Favor & Fleet Share
Manufacturer favor.

You get a small amount of favor for each plane order.

Favor gives passive bonuses; you may alternatively spend it on actions such as instant plane deliveries.

You can undermine the favor between a competitor airline and a manufacturer.

Gain fleet commonality bonuses dependent on what percent of your flying planes belong to a specific manufacturer.

Reduces your in-flight costs

Reduces your maintenance costs

Will also give you bonus favor each day with that manufacturer.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/64a024d76f2b8cc33ca71b66a43712451a22e86c.png"]


New Game Menu Enhancements
Basic View allows you to quickly customize your airline name, choose a preset, and other common tasks.

Airlines View allows you to customize each individual airline before game start.

Advanced View allows you to customize a whole list of new settings. I took a lot of feedback from the community on what sort of things they'd like to see, including things like Aircraft Repair Speed, Manufacturer Research Speed, Aircraft Deprecation and so much more.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/d926a836030b7dd7c439d63cba27f6acd305ec20.png"]
Comfort Improvements
New 'Business' demographic of passengers who only want to sit in business class.

Comfort is now split between seat classes; each seat class has:

A base comfort, which is how comfortable it will be at the start of the game.

A max comfort, which you can try to reach through upgrades and policies.

Starting comforts are: 30 (standing), 55 (economy), 75 (business), 95 (first class).

Airplanes now provide a *comfort bonus* (or penalty). You can conduct body research to try and improve the comfort bonus. This is supposed to be an abstraction of how comfortable the cabin is. Smaller planes will naturally have a lower comfort bonus.

Passengers now have a probability ramp that determines how likely they are to board a given seat.

Budget passengers will always board a seat no matter its comfort.

Comfort passengers will have a 0% chance of boarding below 40 comfort, and a 100% chance above 70 comfort.

Luxury passengers will have a 0% chance of boarding below 70 comfort, and a 100% chance above 110 comfort.

Passengers now have a probability ramp that determines how likely you are to entice them from competitors.

Budget passengers will never switch airlines for comfort reasons.

Comfort, Business and Luxury passengers will switch airlines with 0% chance if comfort differential is less than 5, and 100% chance if comfort differential is more than 20.

Ticket price now only entices budget passengers and some comfort passengers from competitors.

Various policy changes

'Labyrinthine Boarding Groups' now gives +4 comfort to first and business class.

'Free-for-all Boarding' now gives +3 comfort to standing and economy class.

'Free snacks and movies' now gives +3 comfort to all seat classes.

Paid In-flight Restrooms' now gives -6 comfort to all seat classes.

'Free Checked Bags' now gives +3 comfort to all seat classes.

'First Class Experience' now gives +6 comfort to first class.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/bf6739864ed58f4da1ca52b4f7795ae834f6c652.png"]


Network Overview improvements
Airplanes tab: Can now see the route of each airplane

Routes tab: New checkbox to keep the Network Overview open when clicking on "View Route".

Airports tab: Now shows boarding rate and market share. Lets you sort by those two options.

All views now show the count of the thing you have.


Other Features
New option to shuffle city sizes for increased replayability.

New "Expand Airport" button on the Infrastructure GUI panel that allows you to add another building slot.

Your airline now has a CRANE rating. This will affect how eager lenders are to give you money.

There are four new loans available for you to take out.

Whenever manufacturers launch a new model/block, they will offer discounts to each airline on their first 5 or 10 orders.


Changes
Can no longer do priority deals if you are already slated to receive most of the next 15 plane orders.

Priority deal cooldown lowered from an average of ~25 days down to ~18 days.

Priority deal success chance raised from 70% to 80%.

Credits now roll a bit faster, and even faster if you hold down LMB.

Changed how reputation is calculated but made it clearer in the tooltip.

Investing in a production line now gives favor rather than global reputation.

Improved searchbar has come to route manager view. Use tab+enter for easy completion.

Can now search across all developed airports in the route view, even ones that you don't have operating rights in.

Increased fuel efficiency of the Atto from 0.85 to 0.95

Reduced upkeep miles cost from 8/health to 7/health

Inflation is now ~25% of what it used to be. The old "Normal" inflation is now the new "High", for comparison. The idea is to try and increase plane costs and add early-game loans rather than rely on inflation for a more engaging early-mid game.

Rebalanced plane costs; smaller planes increased around ~2x, larger planes between ~3-5x.

Production line base capacity has been nerfed from 8/hr to 6/hr; I felt planes were being built too quickly. But starting efficiency has been boosted to 100% to compensate at least at the immediate start of the game.

Games now start with plane orders pre-populated for the Pico and Veteran. This was done to make game starts more 'fair' by making sure no one airline could hog up all of the planes and choke their competition immediately at the start of the game.

Sawtelle Pico labor unit cost has been reduced from 180 to 120, but miles cost has been bumped from 5000 to 7000.

AI will now be more aggressive in stockpiling planes.

Moderately decreased the cost for manufacturers to open new production lines.

Added a small tooltip to the Hangar view so that if the plane name gets truncated you can still figure out what block it is.

Changing to a conflicting airline policy will now cause a modal window popup.

Buffed standing passenger income from 60% to 85% in order to make up for the new comfort downsides.

Renamed 'creative' mode to 'sandbox' mode to better align with the sim/tycoon genre.

Increased the max tooltip width.


Bugfixes
Fixed bug where nonexistent gates would sometimes randomly pop up for a second or two.

Fixed Puffin Bay Planes Event sometimes giving you planes that had not yet been researched.

Fixed a bug where common infrastructure upgrades done by airports themselves would not be propagated back to the player until save reload or manual upgrade of other infrastructure.

Route manager arrows now show distance even when no plane is selected

Fixed bug where if your airline was named the same as another airline, sometimes you would end up playing their airline after loading a savefile.

Fixed bug where pressing 'DEL' while not having a savefile selected will still trigger the modal window.

Fixed bugs with display of market share in the route card (such as sometimes showing NaN).

Fixed broken achievements (Pico de Gallo, Westside, Flying Fast, Micro on a Macro Scale)

Modal windows now block tooltips.

notes.title: v17: Puffin Planes Planes Update
notes.content:
What's up everybody, I'm back with a new update. This one's been 3 months in the making; I thank everyone on Steam & Discord who gave a ton of feedback and helped make this update fun to play. I'll be putting the game on sale to celebrate the new update, so if you haven't tried the game yet then be sure to check it out!

For this update I really wanted to do a total overhaul of the plane mechanics; I felt that ordering planes kind of lacked depth--you just clicked the button whenever you wanted more of them. So I redid that mechanic and now you need to compete against other airlines to place plane orders! Hopefully this feels more immersive! If you are too lazy to do plane order micromanagement, I also added a used plane marketplace so that you could always have something to fly...although no guarantee that it is in good condition...

That brings me to another new mechanic: plane health! and plane ages! Older planes are harder to maintain. Being in disrepair means that your plane is more likely to crash. You'll now need to make sure you have enough service points to keep your planes in good shape--you can get these by unlocking more airports and building more hangars.

There's a whole set of other features I added such as more planes, plane seating classes, and a reworked policy window. So please give the headlines below a good read, and if you're curious, you can also read the patch notes for other balancing changes and bugfixes. I hope you all enjoy the new update. If you have any ideas for future directions to take the game in, let me know!

Introducing two new birds
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/8f0e989558a2d85c68e14bae3f9d6d7b0f16db2e.png
These birds have special benefits related to the new plane orders and plane maintenance mechanics. 

New planes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/f67028c417ab80139711d0c7d91dee0bcd51f957.png

    Levering Dynamics' lineup now consists of the Veteran, Veteran-ER, and the Roebling.
    Midvale Manufacturing has expanded their lineup to include the PAX-125, Pax-200, PAX-250, PAX-350, PAX-350ER, and PAX-600.
    Sawtelle Heavy Industries' new lineup includes the Atto, Pico, Micro and Macro.

Planes will now gradually unlock throughout the game as the manufacturers research them. Older plane models may sometimes become discontinued, and then after that you will only be able to find them on the used marketplace.

Plane health & aging
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/c3a4901d579b7ca610b74e08e4a7db6d0248b2f0.png

Planes now have an age. Older planes will lose health faster, a.k.a. have more expensive upkeep. Low health will greatly increase crash risk. You can set the maintenance strategy of your airline based on your risk tolerance.
 Fleet Capacity has been replaced with a new Service Points mechanic. You will naturally gain service points over time, and this can be accelerated by unlocking more airports and building maintenance hangars. Planes will consume service points to repair themselves after flights.


New plane ordering system
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/bb6a883958be2b1144d185e42978602733b8fe41.png

 You must now compete with other airlines to order new planes. Don't worry, there's a shiny emergency button to jump the queue (although...you also need to compete to use that).
 You can place orders for the latest block of a given plane; manufacturers will prioritize finishing older blocks, and then those older blocks will be "retired" after all outstanding orders have been completed.
 Manufacturers now control production lines. They will open new production lines if backlogs for any model get too long. They will handle re-assigning production lines between models as needed.


The Great Aircraft Unabstraction
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/f49f8a20d0e54b188ea53db0047f4dd1b669acbb.png
When creating a new route, rather than assigning a model, you now assign...an aircraft! You're playing Puffin Planes after all--not Puffin Plane Models! This ties in nicely with giving individual aircraft ages, etc. to create a more immersive system. In order to provide liquidity, the player has access to the used market, and the ability to spend reputation in order to source more used planes.

Seating Classes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/dfa21788613016ce746c18ffb54c3bb1bcffbc11.png
Some players might call this complexity for complexity's sake. If that's you, then that's fine, I understand. You can honestly just ignore the seating class mechanic entirely and fly all your planes with the "Regional" preset and you will have plenty of fun. But for those of you looking for a bit more immersion, I added the ability to dictate the seating configurations of your plane. Airports vary in their demographics (budget, comfort or luxury) so different configurations may work better or worse in different parts of the world.

Reworked Policies Window
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/742fd8dbed18b745f246b2c8a84094c9b24bc323.png
With the new airplane ordering & upgrade system, I had to get rid of the old tech tree. I hope players find the new mechanics more immersive though! Anyways I slimmed this menu down and added a few more options to choose from.

Full patch notes
v17
Features:
- The Penguin: 2x maintenance speed and -50% service point cost for regular maintenance.
- The Ostrich: 15% chance of receiving an extra plane whenever you take delivery from manufacturer.
- New planes
    - Redone Midvale lineup: PAX-125 (discontinued), PAX-200, PAX-250, PAX-350, PAX-350ER, PAX-600
    - Expanded Sawtelle lineup: Atto (discontinued), Pico, Micro, Macro
    - Expanded Levering lineup: Veteran, Veteran-ER, Roebling
- Planes now have an age. Older planes will lose health faster, a.k.a. have more expensive upkeep.
    - Now receive a notification once per quarter about your old planes.
- Planes will now lose health during flight, especially during takeoff and landing.
    - Low health will greatly increase crash risk.
    - Busy planes may have trouble maintaining themselves.
    - You can set the maintenance strategy of your airline.
    - Having a hangar at an airport will boost maintenance speed.
    - Larger planes now cost 50% more miles to maintain than smaller planes.
- Fleet Capacity has been replaced with a new Service Points mechanic.
    - You will naturally gain service points over time, and this can be accelerated by unlocking more airports and building maintenance hangars.
    - Planes will consume service points to repair themselves after flights.
    - Service points now briefly flash red on navbar when they hit 0
- Airplane Manufacturers. Sawtelle, Midvale and Levering have each been given a neat logo and a little flavor.
    - You will usually see them saving up money but sometimes they might go and open a new production line.
    - They will research new plane models if there are any for them to research.
- New method of ordering planes.
    - Compete with other airlines.
    - Includes a feature to jump the queue.
    - You can now only order the latest block of a given plane.
    - Older blocks will be "retired" after all outstanding orders have been completed.
    - Manufacturers will prioritize finishing outstanding orders for older blocks before moving on to newer ones.
    - New 'Priority Deal' mechanic. Priority Deals are first-come-first-serve and result in any existing orders being moved up in the queue rather than being put into a separate queue.
- Production lines, which are assigned to plane orders.
    - Production lines live on the Investment page.
    - Production lines have cities and randomly generated names.
    - Sabotage or improve the efficiency of the production line.
    - Production lines should slowly reassign to models with busier backlogs (threshold is 2x total length in days)
    - If a new model is researched and there are no production lines to steal, then the manufacturer will go into debt to open a new one.
- New airplane used market.
    - Can now 'find more planes' to immediately source some extra used planes, which will be extra expensive.
    - Planes will now sit on the used market for longer before despawning.
- Blocks. Airplane models have blocks, which determine their stats. You can help research more advanced blocks to improve your planes.
- Seating presets. Choose from available presets or save your own to specify standing, economy, premium and lie-flat seats.
- Passengers now spawn as either Budget, Comfort or Luxury. This determines what seating class(es) they are willing to fly.
- Reworked Policies window. Removed aircraft policies and tried to merge some of them into airline policies.
    - Bold orange text that lets you know that you will overwrite your other choice when switching between conflicting policies.

Changes:
- Hummingbird bonus has been adjusted to a flat 300 km/h bonus to all small plane speeds.
- Tutorial now explains ordering new planes
- Some plane models, such as the PAX-200, can now become obsolete.
- Airplane view in Network Overview now shows the model.
- Debug menu will now show you airports that you have never unlocked before, for help with the Completionist achievement.
- Nerfs to % income policies such as the "Status Program" and "Low Cost Carrier" policies (now just a 2.5% boost across the board except for LCC)
- Nerfed the Puffin % income bonus from 15% to 10%
- Significantly increased crew costs (50% increase); aiming for plane operating costs to be around ~80% of revenue
- ...to compensate, base income is back! Should help you out early game; 500 per day.
- Route Ruler will now by default only show models that you have in your hangar, rather than all models. Configurable.
- Raised the amount of starting miles from 25K to 30K
- Significantly increased most plane prices
- Roebling speed now starts at 1900 kph.
- Unified dropdowns for sorting airplanes across network overview and flight assignment windows.
- Improved the Planes View tooltip to now show you exactly why a plane is taking off or not.
- Pressing 'esc' will now always close sub-windows rather than the parent if open (e.g. select aircraft sub-window).
- Consistent sound effect now plays whenever creating or updating a plane.
- Airport gate view now shows passenger demographics
- Streamlined navbar
- Improved Airplane GUI (and renamed it)
    - Redone location, daily profit and turnaround time badges.
    - Now pick from existing planes rather than model+block combinations; can purchase used planes if desired.
- Can now view your hangar via the renamed "Network & Hangar overview"
- Total rewrite of how aircraft work in the code.
- Aircraft size has been streamlined to 'Small' and 'Large'.
- New passenger spawning algorithm that should be a lot more consistent than the old one. Instead of only trying to spawn between active airports, it tries to spawn between all possible city pairs. This should eliminate issues with one player expanding too fast and hogging all of the passenger spawns.
- All airlines will receive a small base "income" of passengers spawning to make early game more fair.
- Improved End Screen OST by Rod
- Game Over screen now stops music
- Passengers will now refuse to fly crazy routes like Los Angeles -> New York City -> Seattle.
- New warning sign in the route card when you have a significant flow imbalance on a route.
- Next stop pax wait threshold now has two new options, 500+ and 1K+

Bugfixes:
- Fixed bug where planes would not obey the pax count at next stop threshold button.
- Fixed bug where when you buy out another airline, they would still show under the list of who serves each route.
- Fixed a slight bug with the Completionist achievement that could have been affecting some players.
- Fixed a typo in teh "Establish a Hub" contract.
- Fixed bug where destroyed planes were not being handled properly.
- Fixed bug with long runways not being taken into account in some circumstances.
- Fixed bug where AI would try and use tiny planes like the Pico to cross oceans.
- Fixed an ancient bug with repositioning where planes did not take into account planes already flying to the next destination.
- Fixed bug where planes would not depart even when full (apparently an eight month old bug...? confused why it has never been reported until now)
- Fixed a bug with repositioning where planes would try to get a takeoff slot from the first airport of their route, regardless of whether they are repositioning from there or not.
- Fixed the puffinBay event.

notes.title: v17-pre12, pre13
notes.content:
A grab-bag of balance tweaks, bugfixes and small QoL features. We are almost at the finish line--the next patch will probably be a release candidate, with the update out by mid-month.

Changes:

- Some plane models, such as the PAX-200, can now become obsolete.
- Airplane view in Network Overview now shows the model.
- Route ruler now configurable in the settings menu.
- Discontinued models now appear on the 'Models' tab of the Manufacturers GUI.
- Increased fuel efficiency of the Atto to make it easier to break even.
- Route ruler now only shows up if you have planes in your hangar.

- Debug menu will now show you airports that you have never unlocked before, for help with the Completionist achievement.
- If a new model is researched and there are no production lines to steal, then the manufacturer will go into debt to open a new one.
- Moderate (25%-ish) decrease to the price of starter planes

- Plane labor unit cost increases again (sorry I keep going back and forth on this).
- Two new planes, the 'Levering Veteran ER' and the 'Sawtelle Macro'.
- Added some more flavor to production line names.
- Nerfs to % income policies such as the "Status Program" and "Low Cost Carrier" policies (now just a 2.5% boost across the board except for LCC)
- Nerfed the Puffin % income bonus from 15% to 10%
- Significantly increased crew costs (50% increase); aiming for plane operating costs to be around ~80% of revenue
- ...to compensate, base income is back! Should help you out early game; 500 per day.
Bugfixes:
- Route ruler now shows the stats for the highest block that you have.
- Fixed the Midvale PAX-250 research cost being absurdly low for testing purposes.
- Fixed a typo in teh "Establish a Hub" contract.
- Removed references to the abandoned "lease" concept from the game.
- Fixed the 'purchase' button for a new building showing NaN if you had no building selected.
- Fixed being able to create plane if you had enough money to unlock cities, or purchase the used plane, but not both.

v17-pre12
Changes:
- Larger planes now cost 50% more miles to maintain than smaller planes.
- Removed the 'Plane Factory' airport bonus.
- Improved End Screen OST by Rod

- Made some pitiful attempts at game balancing (I swear it's so difficult!)
    - Raised the amount of starting miles from 25K to 30K
    - Significantly increased most plane prices (by 2-3x for many of them)
- Production lines should now slowly reassign to models with busier backlogs (threshold is 2x total length in days)
Bugfixes:
- Fixed airplane costs (fuel, crew, etc) not scaling with inflation (mega facepalm)
- Fixed discontinued planes getting new production lines (e.g. PAX-125)

notes.title: v17-pre8, v17-pre9
notes.content:
I think that this new update is in a pretty good place. Big thanks to everyone on Steam and especially in the Discord who has provided a lot of feedback on how to polish the new plane ordering mechanics. Hopefully this is a step in the right direction. If everything looks good, I will just do a few small tweaks and bugfixes and have the Puffin Planes Planes Update Part 1 out sometime in May.

    - You can now only order the latest block of a given plane.
    - Older blocks will be "retired" after all outstanding orders have been completed.
    - Manufacturers will prioritize finishing outstanding orders for older blocks before moving on to newer ones.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/bb6a883958be2b1144d185e42978602733b8fe41.png

    - Production lines now live on the Investment page.

notes.title: v17-pre6
notes.content:
Just dropping a small [preview] update to get back into the groove of things. I'm hoping to get back to releasing these consistently, life was just really busy over the past month or so.

notes.title: v17-pre5
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/383b76841cc32282ad27efe801526d36ea03c3dd.png

I've been busy but managed to eke out some bugfixes this week as well as a change to seating layouts that I've been mulling in my head for a while. See the picture above--the idea is that casual players will now usually pick one of the 3 default seat classes, but experienced players will be able to min-max as they please using the same percentage mechanics that I have received a lot of positive feedback on.

As always, I'd like to thank everyone for all the feedback I've received. I look forward to going through all of it over the next few weeks as I seek to polish the new mechanics that I've added for the Puffin Planes Planes Update.

v17-pre5
Changes:

notes.title: v16: The AI Update
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=Jr7YDOHk8VM;full][/previewyoutube]

After releasing the game on September 4th, I received an overwhelming amount of encouragement as well as suggestions to make this game even better. I also learned of this little game made back in the 90's called Aerobiz. You might be asking--how in the world did I spend 9 months developing an airline simulator yet never hear of Aerobiz? Well, I guess I didn't do my market research. Also, Aerobiz was released years before I was born. Sorry, I know I just made a few of you feel old.

So based off the feedback I received, I embarked on a journey to make this game even better. Here's a few of the things I tried to address in this massive update:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/80605e55de41dd3268657ea99df4b11fb18ea1be.png

1. Some players thought the game lacked competition. You can now play against AI competitors. You can sabotage them, you can codeshare with them, you can undercut them, and you can even buy them out. I'm sure there's many ways to expand these features in the future, so I'm hoping for some good feedback from y'all.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/edb00a42da6ddf21c51b06524b72b29384b185b1.png

2. Some players felt lke the game wasn't in-depth enough. A lot of the negative reviews I received said that they felt this game was just about drawing lines between airports. They're not wrong, and to address that I tried adding some depth to airports and passengers in this update. You will find a completely re-worked building system at airports, along with a new concourse system for more detailed throughput management at airports. Passengers will now have a preferred airline based on the market share of airlines at their home airport. That is, if you fully control Los Angeles then all passengers that spawn there will be loyal to your airline and prefer flying on it for any layovers.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/7a664a3c668359570f0fbfc497d4459a077d7dd9.png

3. Some players didn't like being railroaded by quarter goals. I originally envisioned this game to be more casual and simplistic, so I thought that the Quarter Goals mechanic would be a perfect fit to give it that Mini Metro/Mini Airways-like feel. However, this mechanic is one of the most common criticisms of the game and so I decided to take the opportunity to rework the reward-punishment system in the new AI update. Now, you will have optional Contracts that will be the new primary way of getting Puffin Tokens. In Hardcore mode, if you don't regularly complete contracts then your CEO Rating can drop to an F, at which point you will be fired. I hope that the contracts system will be more appealing to those who treat this game as a sandbox, while still maintaining the original spirit of the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/2b4d29b34be0a1e989f71bf951b57ff4b587d7fb.png

4. Some players wish they had more statistics available to them. This is very fair. This game has some aspects of a 4X/management game but lacks this one crucial feature in many places. I tried to address that with the new finances GUI, and am hoping that helps a little bit. Obviously there are many places that I can keep working on this in the future.

5. Some players didn't like inflation. The gameplay loop that I envisioned for this game was that inflation would make things progressively more and more expensive until you eventually could not complete your quarter goals anymore, at which point you would fail. Yes, that's right, it's a feature! This is a proven gameplay loop that works for other games like Mini Metro, but it seems people treat my game more seriously and want a more standard management-simulation game loop. So by adding AI competitors and a new win condition (buy them all out), we no longer need crushing inflation to give the player a sense of difficulty.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/4a1aed521c44774bd70aa68f231eee80b2344bbf.png

6. Some players wish there were more achievements. I'm just kidding. But no, really, there are some new achievements.

-----------------------------------------

Thank you to everybody for the support. There is still much that I wish I could have fit into this update, but I think it is better to get it out now and iterate, rather than keeping it stuck in Preview forever. Development will slow down for a month or two as I start a modded Minecraft server with my friends and then go on vacation, however I hope to come back energized next year and see through my vision for this game.

- the developer

notes.title: Developer Diary: Airport Infrastructure Overhaul
notes.content:
Welcome back to another Spontaneous And Completely Unscheduled Developer Diary™. I'm back from my short vacation where I treated myself to some delicious sushi, watched like four different football games on TV, and also went to IKEA at some point. But I know y'all don't care about any of that, so I'll jump right in to this week's topic--the upcoming update's airport infrastructure overhaul.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/1574dc79380b6bf70c341ee3ba391e13b63dcbf0.png

I'll start off with Concourses, which will be a replacement for the current mechanic of buying hub upgrades. Each airport will come with a random number of concourses, with each concourse having a random throughput amount and daily rent. You will be able to upgrade concourses too, although I am still workign out the details and balancing on that. Why did I replace hubs with concourses? Well, it's so you can fight with other players and AI, of course.

Concourses are meant to more realistically model the limited amount of gate space at an airport. Take my home airport of Seattle for example--Delta Airlines mostly occupies concourses A and B, while Alaska Airlines occupies C, D and N. Together, their presence squeezes out any potential third party from establishing a major hub at SeaTac. My hope is that the pressure of fighting over concourses will create similar dynamics in Puffin Planes.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/cfc1da5de326c1eeaaa4da59f4ee077dd2ad61a1.png

Secondly, I have completely overhauled the airport upgrade system by replacing the old upgrade tree with two new types of upgrades: Common Infrastructure and Buildings.

Any money spent to upgrade Common Infrastructure at an airport benefits all airlines. Airports may also spontaneously upgrade their own common infrastructure in certain cases. I'll just go over a few of the new common infrastructure items to give you a sense of the mechanic:

1. Runway length: most airports will start with short runways which don't allow for larger planes such as the PAX-125 to take off and land safely. You can upgrade these to long runways.

2. Runway lighting: most airports will start without runway lighting, which means that takeoff and landing movements will take longer and be more dangerous during the night. Planes of different airlines may accidentally crash into each other.

3. Baggage handling: upgrading this to an automated system will increase base throughput for all airlines at this airport.

Now that I've given you a taste of some of the Common Infrastructure upgrades, let's talk about Buildings. Buildings are the replacement for some of the old upgrade tree items, namely hangars, fuel depots and lounges. Here's a list of some buildings and their effects:

1. Hangars will increase fleet capacity. You will be able to upgrade from a small hangar, to a medium hangar, to a large hangar, to a giant hangar, to a huge hangar, to a mega hangar, to a city-wide hangar, to a planet-wide hangar, to a galactic hangar, to a universal hangar, and eventually to a multidimensional hangar. Just kidding.

2. Hotels will give a permanent boost to market share at an airport. What's market share? Oops, I haven't revealed that yet 🤭. Also, your passengers will wait longer in the preferred state before transitioning into the open state. Oh wait, I haven't talked about what that means yet either, haha. Maybe later this month.

3. Catering facilities will allow you to produce your own meals, lowering your in-flight expenditures.

Have any ideas for buildings or game mechanics that I could try and shove into this update before it drops late this year? Let me know in the replies, the Steam forum or in the Discord.

Hope your September is going well!

notes.title: Beta v15.1: I tried fixing someone's savegame...
notes.content:
I asked a content creator (who I will keep anonymous) for their absolutely massive savefile. They obliged, and I opened it and my computer started stuttering real bad. To be clear, I am running an i7-13700k and 4070 so if a game of Puffin Planes is laggy for me, then it will be laggy for almost everyone.

I got to work over the next couple of days and made dozens of performance improvements that are way too complicated to explain. One of the most important improvements I made was smoothing out lag spikes by distributing the work over multiple frames. This really helped with stability in the massive savefile, which had something like eight hundred planes. Which I will admit is way more than I ever expected anyone to make in my game. But evidently people want to push my game to the limits, and while it was not designed for that...I will do my best to optimize so y'all leave positive reviews upon release hehe.

Also, embarrasingly enough, one of the biggest lag spike was caused by asking the Steam API over and over again if the user had a specific achievement...I added a cache for those references and it really helped make the massive savegame buttery smooth on my machine (OK that may be an exaggeration. But seriously, it is so much better than it was when I first got it).

Oh, and by the way--I fixed that bug that was causing multiplayer games to fail. I tested it by creating a multiplayer game 5 times. Yes, seriously, that's the extent of testing this game gets... the joys of indie dev.

Without further ado, here are the underwhelming patch notes:

notes.title: Beta v14.2: Cool features that many have asked for...
notes.content:
Beta v14.2
Features:
- Can now jump to the region that is your quarter goal in the quarter goal GUIs.
- In Connect Region, etc. quarter goals, the cities that you should be targeting have their name tags highlighted in green for the duration of that quarter.
- You can now pan to the destination airports in the Airport Overview > Demand view. Also clarified that you can click on the connection type portion of each demand view item to make a new route.
- You can now drag onto locked airports and automatically acquire operating rights when starting the plane.
- New Quarter Goal: Build a hub in a region that you underserve. This replaces the old Connect City quarter goal, since generally people did not find that one fun.
- New Quarter Goal: Upgrade Infrastructure at your airports.
- Airplane Marketplace QoL improvement; use SHIFT to order 5x planes at once. use CTRL+SHIFT to order 10.
- New exclamation mark next to "Start Plane" and "Update Plane" to warn you when you are trying to assign a large plane to a route that contains a short runway.

Changes:
- Planes should reposition more intelligently
- Made route lines stand out more when you click on a city
- Airplane Marketplace now shows if a plane is small or large
- In Classic mode, passenger fares will now slowly decay over time to simulate the commoditization of air travel.
- Unlock City and Well Served Routes quarter goals now scale slightly more aggressively
- Added some more flavor to the comet event and made it more common
- Savegames now show more info in the sidebar before you load them
- Distance now shows in the route creator in the airplane GUI, so you can immediately tell how big of a plane you need.
- Renamed "Approach Lighting" to "Instrument Landing"
- Game will now always start paused
- Lowered the fleet capacity per airport served
- Slightly raised the prices of some airport upgrades

Bugfixes:
- Fixed bug where planes would take off early because there are people waiting at the next airport, even if there are still people waiting to board the plane at its current airport.
- Fixed bug where if you loaded a save with 15 minutes left (1 tick) the well-served routes goal would fail. This was actually caused by a more general bug where after loading a save, the first tick would be skipped rather than simulated properly, causing the dataset that the well-served routes goal relies on to not be initialized.
- Fixed the amount of miles you have overflowing if it is an absurdly large number. Seriously, how do you guys manage to make that big of an airline?
- Updated the "Local Time" tooltip in the Airplane Overview
- Fixed achievement descriptions for having 50 Micros and 100 planes (may not update for a while)
- Fixed base income being overwritten by the boost you get from founding an airline
- Fixed reputation dropping at the start of the game before you have any flights
- Fixed tooltip bleedthrough bug
- Attempted to improve the performance of the save/load game GUI by making the save images smaller. It is a 97% reduction in image area, so it should deliver 97% performance increases! Jk. Maybe not quite.

notes.title: Beta v14 makes the game harder!
notes.content:
Beta v14
Features:
- New feature that highlights routes from a specific city when you have it open
- Large airplanes now need a long runway or it will be much more likely for them to crash on takeoff/landing.
- Reworked airport upgrades; added new tree to the left hand side.
- Airports now have a maximum throughput per hour. If you have too many planes trying to load at an airport with low throughput, the planes will be delayed, costing you income and despawning passengers.
- New "Safety Systems" airport bonus. Airports that spawn with this bonus will completely eliminate crashes when flying to and from them.
- Clicking on a plane explosion notification will show a new window where you will have the option to rebuild the plane.
- New UI element in the bottom right quarter that shows you how many of each plane you have under construction.
Changes:
- Slightly increased inflation rates for all levels, and also slightly reduced prices for airplanes to counterbalance in early game.
- Reworked route lines and airplane flight paths to look a little better.
- Removed the ability to favorite planes. This was designed when I originally envisioned the game having dozens of plane models. However since we only have a few to choose from, I have decided to remove the button rather than adding the ability for it to save between loads (and save on clients, etc. if multiplayer)
- Airports now turn yellow if they reach high throughput, as a suggestion that something is Not Quite Right.
- Locked airports are now white instead of yellow, and are transparent to differentiate from unlocked airports.
- Efficient Operations now provides a boost to throughput instead of a reduction in landing fee.
- Tabbed windows now default to the last opened tab when you open them again. Let me know if you think there are situations where this behavior should not be true.
- Buffed how much Attractive Career Benefits reduces your risk of plane crashes (from 2x to 5x)
- Policies & Upgrades GUI now shows you how many tokens you have available to spend in the bottom right corner.
- Made the text in the Quarter Goal Overview bigger
- Game will now auto-pause at the start if the tutorial is enabled, for new players
Bugfixes:
- Fixed bug where profitability mapmode icon would not highlight when you are viewing that mapmode
- Fixed bug where selecting "Quit to Desktop" would go to the main menu instead.
- Fixed the not-workingness of the buttons that let you select plane max waiting time, next stop takeoff thresholds.
- Fixed bug where updating plane max wait time would instead update next stop pax waiting threshold.
- Fixed the name of Montevideo in Uruguay

notes.title: Beta v13 bugfixes
notes.content:
Beta v13.4
Bugfixes:
- Fixed bug that would cause savegame loads to fail for users with slower computers.

Beta v13.3
Features:

- New option to disable/enable explosions and camera shake.
- New algorithm for calculating how much a passenger pays out per stop. This will make long-haul routes appear more profitable, although it does not fundimentally change the ticket price of a flight.

- Fixed bug where having an ancient save game would wreak havoc on your ability to play the game
- Fixed bug where you would be unable to join a multiplayer game as client
- Fixed the Westside achievement being unachievable
- Fixed bug where planes would not be destroyed after you decommissioned them
- Fixed the North Carolina achievement not recognizing you flying out of Raleigh-Durham
- Fixed sometimes not having enough airports available early-game to exceed certain quarter goals.

- Fixed Southern Cross achievement being unachieveable.

notes.title: Beta v13: Achievements & Incidents
notes.content:
Beta v13
Features:
- Planes can now crash; new setting to determine plane crash frequency, and it is also affected by fleet capacity and policies.
- Implemented achievements. Please let me know if you run into any bugs with these.
- Routes now show how many passengers are transported over them per day, on average.

- Comfort now affects reputation
- Search City GUI now auto-selects on enable, and you can now submit via enter.

- Fixed bug in calculating chart size
- Fixed bug in statistics chart where it would not render the points correctly.
- Fixed bug in statistics chart where it would break when trying to render charts with values under 10.
- Fixed bug where airports will appear in their own Demand tabs as "Difficult Connection"
- Fixed bug with displayed calculation of landing fee in the airport window, and clarified it.

notes.title: Beta v12.1: Bugfixes
notes.content:
Beta v12.1
Features:
Changes:
- Slightly increased passenger spawn rate on Earth and decreased it on Mars.
- Lowered the Well Served Routes goal difficulty, especially at the beginning of the game.
Bugfixes:
- Fixed bug where users would be unable to see the number of passengers waiting at the ends of a route.
- Fixed critical bug where loading a save game will cause the Expand to Region Quarter Goal to break.
- Fixed New Orlando not having a region on Mars.

notes.title: Beta v12: The Performance Update
notes.content:
Beta v12
Features:
- Significantly reduced bandwidth usage in multiplayer. Up to 90% reduction while paused, 75% reduction at Speed 1 and 50% reduction at Speed 2.
- Significant late-game performance improvements. In my testing, tick times were decreased by over 70%. This does not correlate directly with FPS, but combined with the bandwidth improvements it should mean that you can play at least twice as long as before without running into performance issues.
- Significant performance improvements to the Network Overview--should no longer lag even in late-game.
- Significant performance improvements to the Airport GUI (gate view and expansion view).
- Can now use the 'ESC' key to close most menus.
- New setting for choosing between 'Windowed', 'Fullscreen Window (Borderless)' and 'Exclusive Fullscreen'
Changes:
- Now that there have been significant performance improvements, I have increased the speed of the game. In Speed 1 ticks now occur every 500ms (down from 600ms) and in Speed 2 they occur every 250ms (down from 300ms).
Bugfixes:
- Fixed spacebar causing some UI elements to change.
- Fixed the lag between clicking to unlock an airport, and the airport actually unlocking. Should help in multiplayer late-game. This also fixes a weird bug where sometimes trying to drag right after you unlock an airport will result in the world moving.
- Fixed bug where the amount of miles you were awarded would overflow and become negative in late-late game.
- Fixed bug where Planes view in the airport window would never scroll.
- Policies and Upgrades overlay GUI now properly moves to the front of the GUI when you open it, rather than having other windows such as the Airport GUI appear over it.

notes.title: Beta v11.1 - Bugfixes and tweaks
notes.content:
Beta v11.1
Changes:
- Connect City Quarter Goal will now never ask you to connect a given city to more than 5 other cities.
- Connect City Quarter Goal will now choose from a wider range of cities instead of just those with 2 or less gates.
- Unlock City Quarter Goal will now be less aggressive.
- Developed airport icon clicks now occur before route line clicks.
Bugfixes:
- City distance cache now resets between savegames.
- Marketplace GUI now checks for newly unlocked planes much more frequently.
- Improved Polish city names on Mars. Thanks Avalanche!

notes.title: Beta v11: Welcome to Mars
notes.content:
Beta v11
Features:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/9f73e9b409a2f7441ad8f305f67a2baa4523eb96.jpg
- Mars. In early testing! Please give some feedback and let me know if you have any country or city ideas.
- Quarter goals now have "Meets Expectations" and "Exceeds Expectations" categories. Reaching "Exceeds Expectations" will give you extra bonuses.
- Redesigned Network Overview now with 3 tabs for Airplanes, Airports and Routes.
- New route option: "Max Wait Time". You can now configure the maximum duration a plane will wait at an airport before taking off.
- New route option: "Next Stop Passenger Count Threshold". You can now configure a threshold of people waiting at this plane's next stop that, if reached, will cause the plane to take off.
Changes:
- Airports will now spawn slightly more frequently.
- Now only need to unlock 3 cities for the first quarter, with 5 for exceeds expectations.
- "How about some planes?" option for the Quarter Goal Accomplished Event is now exclusive to "Exceeds Expectations".
- Reduced quarter goal bonuses for "Meets Expectations".
- Re-added the taglines to the main menu.
- Plane range now appears when hovering over the route arrow, rather than the route item.
Bugfixes:
- Fixed a bug where if you clicked on a city while in the Airplane overview menu, the "ghost" plane will remain visible.
- Fixed a bug where if you tried to change the route of a plane that was under construction, it would appear as if the route had never changed.
- Fixed out-of-date Puffin Token text.
- Fixed bug where route statistics did not save/load properly.
- Disabled warning in TextMeshPro that led to characters not supported by my font polluting the logs with error messages.
- Fixed bug where notifications would not work properly on the client.
- Massive code changes behind the scenes to support multiple planets and more dynamic airports. I'm not kidding when I say that these code changes are where the majority of this update's time was spent.

What's Next

In the Discord, I asked and the answer was loud and clear--y'all want some late game performance improvements, and additional content polishing. So those two things will be my focus for the month of July! Stay tuned.

notes.title: Beta v10: Skill Tree Update
notes.content:
Beta v10
Features:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/e624c6e8738c37fe15b6c3b94e597b0f72eee11a.jpg
- Completely reworked Airplane Upgrades: now located in a new 'Policies and Upgrades' window, with stronger and more unique bonuses.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/05d4b1b11ba7fbddaa491f1213d7abc1245f651b.jpg
- Completely reworked Airport Upgrades: now follows a skill tree like Airplane Upgrades. Costs miles instead of Puffin Tokens.

- Airline Policies: located in the 'Policies and Upgrades' window, allows you to specialize your airline.
- Autosaves! Configure how often you want them (or turn them off) in the settings menu under 'Other'.
- Note that there is a KNOWN BUG with autosaves where you will not get the Quarter Goal Accomplished Event (which gives you the option of miles, Puffin Tokens, etc.) when loading an autosave. I am working on a fix for this however it will require major changes behind the scene. Since autosaves are not a critical feature I am leaving this in place so that everything else can be tested.
- Creative Mode with infinite miles and tokens, and planes build instantly.
- Can now see how profitable a route is with tooltips and new Profitability mapmode.
Changes:
- The "How about some planes?" event in the Quarter Goal Accomplished Event has been buffed and will now give more high-value planes much more frequently.
- Quit to desktop now asks if you want to save any unsaved changes first.
- Second quarter goal is now always either Unlock New City or Well Served Routes, so that it is easier to get established.
- Larger planes now take up less fleet capacity, making them more efficient.
- Fleet capacity is now easier to get, and the penalties for exceeding it are steeper.
- The higher your reputation, the more likely you are to get an extra Puffin Token during the new fiscal quarter in Classic mode.
- Revamped Airplane Marketplace
- New Puffin Token icon.
- UI buttons now colored for easier differentiation.
- Added expanding animation to some buttons. Let me know if you feel this is annoying.
- Airport Icons now require more passengers before they start animating.
- Reworked the Plane Improvement Event to now just give you a Puffin Token, and be less common.
- Now receive more Miles from the quarterly goal options.
- Now can receive only up to two Puffin Tokens from the quarterly goal options.
- Average trip length is now more lenient when affecting your reputation. The "zero point" (above which it decreases your reputation, and below which it increaeses) has been moved from 2.5 to 3.0.
Bugfixes:
- Airplanes in hangar were not counting towards total fleet capacity used for calculating upkeep cost.

notes.title: Beta v9: The QoL before the storm
notes.content:
Hello Puffin Planes players! This is a small update to address a few bugs as well as improve your QoL while playing the game. I am putting this out now so that I can focus on the Airplane and Airline skill tree update in the next few weeks. Don't know what that is? Join the Discord to get a sneak peak!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002107/6a49e765007e47634c6dc62f015c372c2b4164a3.jpg
New chart: Average Trip Length

Beta v9
Features:
- Can now force send the plane to its next destination. Intended to help players manually rebalance longer routes.
- Passenger spawn rate is now configurable
- New charts: Avg. Trip Length and Score.
- Can now use the +/- keys to zoom in and out.
- Plane contrails now scale based on how full a plane is. Empty planes will have no contrails, while full planes will have long contrails.
- Cities now have a "heartbeat" that is based on how many people are waiting there.
Changes:
- Charts now scale following the pattern '10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, ...' rather than '10, 100, 1000, ...' to be more gentle.
- Your score is now affected by passenger trip length. If you take many flights to deliver a passenger to their final destination, you will get less score.
- Connecting flights no longer increase the total ticket price a passenger is willing to pay. This was causing an exploit where it was more profitable to make connecting flights. It was originally added to subsidize the early-game however this is no longer necessary because of other superior early game balancing solutions.
- "New Plane" is now "Click to add new plane" in Route Card.
- Tweaks to the Airplane UI to fix spacing, graphics issues and better-promote hierarchy for new players who often miss the "Assign Plane" button.
Bugfixes:
- Fixed a bug where using multi-routes would break plane repositioning.
- Fixed a bug where multi-routes would break the calculations for the Well-served Routes goal.

notes.title: Beta v8: Play the Demo, Massive Performance Fixes, and New Mapmode
notes.content:
PLAY THE DEMO! Visit the Steam page and download the Demo now.

Did your savegame break? That's expected in development. But fear not--you can go to Properties -> Betas and install the legacy version, which will always be the previous update!

Beta v8
Features:
- Redid all achievement icons to have a cohesive art style.
- New "Number of Passengers Waiting" mapmode that colors routes based off of how many passengers are waiting at both ends.
- Can now load savefiles in multiplayer.
- Significant late-game performance optimizations
Changes:
- Added some more bird names.
- Can now control movement and zoom speed. Thanks avalanche!
- Increased the role that distance+nationality plays on passenger spawning. For example, passengers from the EU will now mostly travel within the EU, rather than a large portion of them wanting to go to the Congo.
- Increased the base passenger spawn rate by 37.5%. This should boost starts in poorer regions of the world and lead to a more balanced early-game. Thanks avalanche and Bearwolf!
- Returning to Main Menu will now prompt you to confirm if you have not saved the game. Thanks Bearwolf!
- Reduced bandwidth usage by 14%
- Reputation now affects the type of events you get. Positive reputation will make positive events more likely, while negative reputation will increase the frequency of negative events.
- Airport icons on map now display region and country.
- Unlock City Popup now displays country.
- Inflation is slightly reduced across the board, but especially for High inflation rate.
- Game will now start paused when loading multiplayer games.
- A lot of refactoring happened behind the scenes. This helps make sure that the game is in a good place for future features and additions.
- Nerfed the range of the Sawtelle Micro.
- Rebalanced Unlock City and Well-served Routes quarter goals.
- Faraway cities now unlock more often.
- Made Expand to Region Quarter Goal more common.
Bugfixes:
- Portugal is now in Southern Europe, rather than Western Europe.
- Fixed a bug where unlocked airports would carry over between games.
- Fixed a bug where windows would open in weird places if you changed the UI scale mid-game.
- Fixed a bug where you cannot play Singleplayer after playing Multiplayer, or vice versa, without restarting the game.
- Fixed being able to click on Perk Badges to upgrade perks even when perks were already at maximum level or when you did not have any Puffin Tokens.
- Fixed issue where Airplane Marketplace would sometimes not open. Thanks avalanche!
- Fixed bug where the number of cities you have already unlocked in a region would not be taken into account when deciding which region to target for a Expand to Region quarter goal.
- Will no longer develop airports in cities literally right next to your existing cities (min. dist is now 175km)
- The amount of money you get on new quarters is now adjusted for inflation.

notes.title: Beta v7: The Multiplayer Update
notes.content:
Finally! Built-in Multiplayer Host/Join support. Also, today I completed the demo for Puffin Planes, which I will release sometime in the next few weeks.

notes.title: Beta v6: The Expansion QoL Update
notes.content:
Beta v6
Features:
- Can now view the most in-demand destinations from a given city! Click on the 'Expansion' tab when viewing a city. Special thanks to Drew Durnil for feedback on how difficult it is to find out who wants to go where.
- New Search GUI accessible from the navbar that lets you find your favorite cities.

- New Airplane Chime sound effect
- There is now a Legend in the statistics view.
- New "Plane Improvement" event. Offers you a random free perk on one of your unlocked plane models.

- Renamed "Fund Expansion" to "Donate Funds" since Expansion is now a new tab in the Airport menu.
- Decreased inflation for all difficulties. Prices will be slightly higher in early game, but significantly lower mid and late game.
- Airline GUI now shows each airline's color.
- Airline GUI now has space for up to 8 airlines without scrolling.
- Can now convert a game to freeplay mode after Game Over.

As always, you can reach me on the Discord or Twitter.

notes.title: Beta v3/v4/v5
notes.content:
Beta v3, v4 and v5 were released over the past week and a half. The pace of updates will slow down a little bit and their scope will grow larger from here on out.

Beta v5
Features:
- Statistics View: New view that shows you daily profit, etc. Check it out on the navbar! Loading a pre-Beta v4 save game will lead to some stats being set to zero.
- Charts! Watch your Miles balance go up over time in the new navbar chart. See the number of people waiting at an airport.
Changes:
- Unlock City and Well-Served Route Quarter Goals made easier.
- Decreased costs to unlock new cities
- Increased income per-passenger
Bugfixes:
- Pressing spacebar will no longer randomly close windows opened from the navbar.
- Client and Server now agree what day it is.

Beta v4
Features:
- South is up: New setting that allows you choose whether north or south is up. Australians rejoice!
Changes:
- Fixed bug in tooltip of the Tourist Hotspot Developed event
- Slightly nerfed income
- Bonuses are now twice as rare on average. Some effects have been boosted to compensate.
- Unlock City and Well Served Routes quarter goals now no longer scale based on how many cities or routes you already have. This is because players complained of feeling disincentivized to unlock more cities if they had already reached the quarter goal with time to spare.
- Inflation is now configurable when starting a new game.
- Main menus are now slightly wider.
- Can now right-click to delete all of your airline's planes on a route.
Bugfixes:
- If a new quarter happens while you have an airplane window open, it will no longer un-select the airplane's currently selected model.
- Noumea is no longer in Western Europe

Beta v3
Features:
- Quarter Goal Icon: the cities that are subjects of your quarter goal will get a helpful icon. City tooltip should now be more helpful too.
- Draggable windows: drag windows wherever you'd like!
- Tourist destination: new airport bonus that increases demand to and from the airport. Added an event that can randomly create tourist destinations during the game.
- Freeplay Mode: can now play without the stress of accomplishing quarterly goals! Two puffin tokens will automatically be deposited into your airline per quarter.
Changes:
- Planes disappear slightly earlier in their flight paths so that they don't conflict with trying to click on an airport.
- Passengers now wait a little longer before despawning.
- Soundtrack now plays in-game. New Music slider in the game settings.
- New Discord and Twitter links in main menu.
- Added a small delay before the tooltip becomes active. So when rapidly moving your mouse from one end of the screen to the other, you should get a more minimalist, zen-like feel.
- Now get a tick-tock sound effect when you are approaching the end of the quarter and you have not accomplished your goal.
- Increased the amount of money you are offered as part of the quarter goal completed events.
- Plane tooltips now show transfer profit so you can better tell unprofitable routes from transfer workhorse routes.
- Hitting escape now pauses the game in singleplayer.
- UI improvements to the Airplane Overview. And can now favorite/unfavorite models in that menu.
Bugfixes:
- Hotkeys, such as spacebar or WASD, no longer have an effect when in the escape menu.
- Default settings now work properly for new settings that your settings.json file has never seen before.
- Any active right click menu will now close when hitting escape or triggering a modal.
